questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added under which part of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part IVA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• They are enshrined under **Part IVA** of the Constitution of India, specifically in **Article 51A**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were introduced based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**, which was constituted in 1976.
 
• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties, but the **86th Amendment Act, 2002**, added one more duty, making a total of 11 Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Fundamental Duties apply to all Indian citizens and are aimed at promoting a sense of responsibility and commitment towards the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IV**

 
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution deals with the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**.
 
• The DPSPs are non-justiciable guidelines provided to the state to ensure socio-economic welfare and justice.
 
• Examples include provisions for securing a living wage, equitable distribution of resources, and promotion of educational and economic interests of weaker sections.
 
• They are included in Articles 36 to 51.
 
 
 
• **Part VIA**
 
 
• Part VIA does not exist in the Indian Constitution.
 
• This option might have been presented as a distractor in the question.
 
 
 
• **Part VI**
 
 
• Part VI of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions related to the **States in India**.
 
• It includes Articles 152 to 237, which specify the structure, powers, and functions of the state governments.
 
• It encompasses the Governor, State Legislature, High Courts, and subordinate courts.
 
• Part VI does not deal with Fundamental Duties.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the government's fiscal policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To ensure maximum employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy. The primary goal is to achieve economic stability and growth.
 
• One of the main objectives of fiscal policy is to ensure maximum employment by stimulating economic activities and creating job opportunities.
 
• Governments often increase spending on infrastructure, health, education, and other sectors to boost employment levels.
 
• Fiscal policy also includes tax cuts or incentives for businesses to encourage investment and hiring.
 
• By ensuring maximum employment, fiscal policy contributes to reducing income inequality and improving the standard of living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Main Tools of fiscal policy:**

 
 
• Government Spending: Direct spending on infrastructure, defense, education, etc., or transfer payments.
 
• Taxation: Adjusting income tax, corporate tax, sales tax, etc., to influence spending and investment.
 
• Public Debt Management: Borrowing and managing government debt levels. 
 
 
 
• **Types of Fiscal Policy**
 
 
• Expansionary: Used during recessions; involves increased spending or tax cuts to boost demand, output, and employment.
 
• Contractionary (Deflationary): Used to fight inflation; involves reduced spending or higher taxes to decrease demand.

questions.question: Which five-year plan focused on food, work and productivity?

__
 
• The **Seventh Five-Year Plan** of India was operational from **1985 to 1990** and focused on improving food production, generating employment opportunities, and enhancing productivity.
 
• Its main objective was to achieve a **self-sustained economy**, emphasizing modernization of agriculture and rural development.
 
• The plan aimed to achieve a target growth rate of **5% annual GDP growth**, but it surpassed expectations by achieving approximately 6% growth.
 
• It introduced **programs like Jawahar Rozgar Yojana**, focusing on employment generation in rural areas.
 
• This plan also laid special focus on **social justice and reducing poverty** by improving the living standards of the poor.

• The focus was on poverty reduction, employment generation, and technological self-reliance.
 
• This plan emphasized the removal of poverty through the **Integrated Rural Development Program (IRDP)**.
 
• It also aimed to achieve economic growth through industrial modernization and agricultural development.
 
• The concept of **Minimum Needs Program** was introduced to improve living standards by providing essential facilities like education, healthcare, and drinking water.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1978)**
 
 
• The main focus was on **poverty alleviation** and achieving self-reliance in agricultural and industrial production.
 
• It introduced programs like the **Minimum Needs Program** and **Garibi Hatao** (Eradicate Poverty) to address socio-economic inequalities.
 
• Due to political instability, the plan was terminated in 1978, one year before its scheduled completion.
 
 
 
• **Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992-1997)**

• The plan aimed to reduce fiscal deficits, encourage privatization, and promote industrial growth.

questions.question: Animals where the fertilisation of eggs and the development of the baby up to the fetal stage takes place inside the mother's body are known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**viviparous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Animals that give birth to live young ones and where fertilization occurs internally are classified as **viviparous animals**.
 
• In viviparous animals, the embryo develops inside the mother’s body, and nourishment is provided through a placenta or other internal structures.
 
• Examples of viviparous animals include most mammals, such as humans, lions, and whales.
 
• Viviparity ensures better protection and survival chances for the offspring as they develop in a controlled internal environment.
 
• Viviparous reproduction is an advanced evolutionary adaptation compared to oviparity (egg-laying), as it increases the likelihood of offspring survival in challenging environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oviparous**

 
 
• Oviparous animals lay eggs, and the development of the embryo occurs outside the mother’s body.
 
• Fertilization can occur either internally (e.g., birds, reptiles) or externally (e.g., fish, amphibians).
 
• Examples include hens, frogs, snakes, and fish.
 
• Oviparity is common in species where external environmental factors provide suitable conditions for egg development.
 
 
 
• **Vertebrates**
 
 
• Vertebrates are animals that possess a backbone or spinal column.
 
• They belong to the phylum Chordata and include classes such as mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fish.
 
• Both oviparous and viviparous animals can be vertebrates.
 
• Examples include humans, snakes, frogs, and sharks.
 
 
 
• **Invertebrates**
 
 
• Invertebrates are animals that lack a backbone or spinal column.
 
• This group includes animals such as insects, arachnids, mollusks, crustaceans, and sponges.
 
• Most invertebrates are oviparous, though there are some exceptions.
 
• Examples include octopuses, spiders, and jellyfish.

questions.question: In which functional group is the carbonyl carbon attached to the hydrogen atom as well as to the carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aldehyde**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An aldehyde is an organic compound in which the carbonyl carbon is bonded directly to a hydrogen atom and an alkyl or aryl group (R group).
 
• The general formula for aldehydes is **R-CHO**, where R represents an alkyl or aryl group.
 
• The carbonyl group (C=O) in aldehydes is highly reactive, making aldehydes important intermediates in organic synthesis.
 
• Aldehydes are commonly found in nature, often as components of essential oils, flavoring agents, and fragrances (e.g., formaldehyde, benzaldehyde).
 
• Some aldehydes, like formaldehyde, are widely used in industrial applications such as resins, plastics, and disinfectants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amides:**

 
 
• Amides are organic compounds containing the functional group **-CONH2**, where the carbonyl group (C=O) is attached to a nitrogen atom (NH2).
 
• They are derived from carboxylic acids by replacing the hydroxyl group (-OH) with an amino group (-NH2).
 
• Amides are important in biological systems, such as in the structure of proteins where peptide bonds are formed between amino acids.
 
• Examples include acetamide (CH3CONH2) and benzamide (C6H5CONH2).
 
 
 
• **Carboxylic Acids:**
 
 
• Carboxylic acids are organic compounds characterized by the presence of a carboxyl group (-COOH).
 
• The carboxyl group contains a carbonyl group (C=O) attached to a hydroxyl group (-OH).
 
• Carboxylic acids are weak acids and are widely found in nature, such as acetic acid (vinegar) and citric acid (citrus fruits).
 
• They are used in the production of polymers, pharmaceuticals, and food additives.
 
 
 
• **Ketones:**
 
 
• Ketones are organic compounds in which the carbonyl group (C=O) is attached to two alkyl or aryl groups.
 
• The general formula for ketones is **R-CO-R'**, where R and R' are alkyl or aryl groups.
 
• Ketones are used in various applications, including solvents (acetone), fragrances, and intermediates in chemical synthesis.
 
• Unlike aldehydes, ketones do not have a hydrogen atom directly attached to the carbonyl group.

questions.question: Which of the following water bodies typically has the highest salinity (dissolved salts)?

__
 
• **Ocean water has the highest salinity** among natural water bodies, typically ranging from 34 to 36 parts per thousand (ppt), as it contains dissolved salts like sodium chloride, magnesium, and calcium.
 
• The salinity of oceans is primarily influenced by evaporation, precipitation, river inflow, and ocean currents. High evaporation rates in tropical regions result in higher salinity levels.
 
• **Dead Sea and certain areas of the Red Sea** are examples of regions with exceptionally high salinity due to minimal freshwater inflow and high evaporation rates.
 
• Marine organisms have adapted to high salinity levels, making oceans crucial for biodiversity and ecological balance.
 
• Oceans cover approximately 71% of Earth's surface and play a significant role in regulating the planet's climate and hydrological cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pond**

 
 
• Ponds are small, shallow freshwater bodies with low salinity levels as they primarily accumulate rainwater and runoff.
 
• They often support various aquatic plants and animals but are not significant contributors to global salinity levels.
 
• The salinity in ponds can increase due to pollution or lack of freshwater inflow but remains much lower than in oceans.
 
 
 
• **River**
 
 
• Rivers are freshwater systems with **negligible salinity** (typically less than 0.5 ppt), as they are primarily fed by precipitation, snowmelt, or springs.
 
• They transport dissolved minerals and salts to oceans, contributing to ocean salinity.
 
• Human activities like agriculture and industrial discharge can increase salinity levels in certain river systems.
 
 
 
• **Lake**
 
 
• Most lakes are freshwater bodies with **low salinity**, but saltwater lakes such as the Great Salt Lake or Lake Van can have high salinity due to evaporation and lack of outflow.
 
• The salinity levels in lakes vary based on geographical location, climate, and surrounding geological formations.

questions.question: The area of a triangle is constant. Find the percentage increase in its perpendicular height if the base of the triangle is decreased by 20%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the product of two variables is constant, and one variable decreases by x%, the other must increase by [x / (100 − x)] × 100%.

Here, the base decreases by 20%, so x = 20.

Percentage increase in height = [20 / (100 − 20)] × 100%

⇒ (20 / 80) × 100% = (1 / 4) × 100% = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The area of the triangle is constant.

The base is decreased by 20%.

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height

 Constant Area: Base × Height = Constant
 
 Base: 100
 

 

 −20%
 
 New Base: 80
 
 Height: 80
 

 

 +25%
 
 New Height: 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial base be b and the initial height be h.

⇒ Initial Area = 1/2 × b × h

⇒ New base = b − 20% of b = 0.8b

⇒ Let the new height be H.

⇒ New Area = 1/2 × 0.8b × H

⇒ Since the area remains constant: 1/2 × b × h = 1/2 × 0.8b × H

⇒ b × h = 0.8b × H

⇒ H = h / 0.8 = 10/8 × h = 1.25h

⇒ Increase in height = 1.25h − h = 0.25h

⇒ Percentage increase = (0.25h / h) × 100% = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Product Rule

If A × B = Constant, a decrease of a/b in quantity A requires an increase of a/(b−a) in quantity B. Here, 20% = 1/5 decrease in base, which directly requires a 1/(5−1) = 1/4 = 25% increase in height.

Successive Percentage Change

When two variables change by a% and b%, the net percentage change in their product is given by: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) / 100. For the area to remain constant, the net change must be 0%.

Area of a Triangle

The foundational formula for the area of any triangle is 1/2 × Base × Perpendicular Height. Altering the base and height in strictly inverse proportions will always keep the overall area completely unchanged.
</p

questions.question: Let x be the greatest number which, when divided by 31, 61 and 91, leaves the same remainder. The LCM of x and 48 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The greatest number leaving the same remainder is the HCF of the differences of the given numbers.

Differences: (61 − 31) = 30, (91 − 61) = 30, (91 − 31) = 60.

x = HCF(30, 30, 60) = 30.

Required LCM = LCM(30, 48).

Since 30 = 6 × 5 and 48 = 6 × 8, LCM = 6 × 5 × 8 = 240.

**∴ The correct answer is 240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 31, 61, and 91.

x is the greatest number that leaves the same remainder when dividing these numbers.

**Formula Used:**

If a number leaves the same remainder when dividing a, b, and c, then the greatest such number is the HCF of |a − b|, |b − c|, and |c − a|.

**Calculation:**

⇒ First difference = 61 − 31 = 30

⇒ Second difference = 91 − 61 = 30

⇒ Third difference = 91 − 31 = 60

⇒ x = HCF of 30, 30, and 60

⇒ x = 30

⇒ We need to find the LCM of x and 48, which is the LCM of 30 and 48.

⇒ Prime factorization of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 48 = 2⁴ × 3

⇒ LCM(30, 48) = highest power of each prime factor present

⇒ LCM(30, 48) = 2⁴ × 3 × 5 = 16 × 15 = 240

**∴ The correct answer is 240.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest Number Dividing with Same Remainder

When asked for the greatest number that divides a, b, and c leaving the same remainder, compute the HCF of their absolute differences: |a − b|, |b − c|, and |c − a|.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is exactly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is found by multiplying the highest power of all prime factors involved.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is the product of the lowest power of each common prime factor.
</p

questions.question: Find the fourth proportional of 4, 6 and 5.

For any three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional (d) can be found directly using the formula:

d = (b × c) ÷ a

Here, a = 4, b = 6, and c = 5.

Fourth proportional = (6 × 5) ÷ 4 = 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5

**∴ The correct answer is 7.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 4

Second term (b) = 6

Third term (c) = 5

**Formula Used:**

If four values a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then the ratio of the first two equals the ratio of the last two.

⇒ a ÷ b = c ÷ d

⇒ Product of Extremes (a × d) = Product of Means (b × c)

**Calculations:**

Let the fourth proportional be x.

⇒ 4 : 6 :: 5 : x

⇒ 4 ÷ 6 = 5 ÷ x

⇒ 4 × x = 6 × 5

⇒ 4x = 30

⇒ x = 7.5

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is the square root of their product. It is given by x = √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion such that a : b :: b : c, then c is called the third proportional, given by c = b² ÷ a.

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If two ratios are equal such that a ÷ b = c ÷ d, then applying Componendo and Dividendo gives (a + b) ÷ (a − b) = (c + d) ÷ (c − d).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• वाक्य - परिणामस्वरूप, 1977 में पहली बार सत्ता **परिवर्तन__** हुआ।
 
• वाक्य में 'परिवर्तन' शब्द का प्रयोग सत्ता में बदलाव को दर्शाता है, जो 1977 के गठबंधन सरकार के संदर्भ से मेल खाता है।
 
• 'परिवर्तन' का अर्थ - बदलाव या रूपांतरण।

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**अन्य विकल्प -

 
• **'स्थायित्व'** का अर्थ - स्थिरता।
 
• **'विकेंद्रीकरण'** का अर्थ - शक्ति का वितरण।
 
• **'स्थानांतरण'** का अर्थ - स्थान परिवर्तन।
